الرَّجَّافُ The sea; because of its commotion, or agitation. (S, O, K.) A poet says, (S,) namely, Matrood Ibn-Kaab, lamenting the death of ' Abdel-Muttalib, (IB, O,) the grandfather of the Prophet, and eulogizing him, (IB,) “اَلْمُطْعِمُونَ الشَّحْمَ كُلَّ عَشِيَّةٍ
حَتَّى تَغِيبَ الشَّمْسُ فِى الرَّجَّافِ
” [The feeders with fat every evening, until the sun disappeared in the sea]. (S, O.) ―
-b2- And The day of resurrection: (Sh, O, K:) and the congregation [of the risen]. (K.) ―
-b3- And رَجَّافٌ also signifies A certain kind of pace [app. with a jolting motion]. (O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
